subject: filecabinet
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: filecabinet.mdl, in the place of the game's models/filecabinet.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_gauss.mdl, models/w_oxygen.mdl, models/w_suit.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 3 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, B where the asset was C, A, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: In all six sides (front, left, back, right, top, below) and the four angles, the outline is one upright box with a slightly wider top lip and a darker plinth at the base, matching a three-drawer filing cabinet. No part sticks out or is missing. The silhouette overlap was not measured numerically, so this is judged by eye.

M2.reason: Measured size 28.8 x 22.6 x 62.4 against the brief's 29 deep, 23 wide and 62 high. Each dimension is within 1% (sizeOff 0.008).

M3.reason: Brief parts: three drawers, a handle on each drawer, a top, a base. The front view shows three drawer fronts stacked from top to bottom, each with a dark painted pull in its centre; the pulls read clearly in the front view and as dark marks in the line-up at its size. The top lip and plinth are present in the front and side-angle views. There are no round parts or small attachments in the brief to miscount.

M4.reason: The brief asks for grey steel. The whole body is a mid grey with a mottled darker grime over it, and the drawer fronts and top share that colour. The handles are a darker painted metal, as the brief implies. No region is a different material or a clearly different colour.

M5.reason: The brief asks for a bit of grime. Darker blotches and a fine speckle sit across the sides, back and top, in the places one would expect for worn steel. Drawer edges and the recessed drawer lines are drawn in the front view. The left view has a faint tall panel line, which is minor and does not count against the brief.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test, as the rubric requires. The asset sat at C, A and D in the three orders. Judges picked D, D and B, so each reading picked a Valve model over the asset, and the asset passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The drawer fronts face the front view, the cabinet stands upright on its flat base with no tilt, and the plinth sits on the origin as a filing cabinet would. The back, sides and top match that orientation.

M8.reason: The checks report no errors. It has 14 triangles, well under twice the median (238) and under the third quartile (291) of Half-Life's props of its kind. In every view the box is closed: no side, top or underside is open or inside out, and the base sits on the ground.
